To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tip-to-base distribution of CaM was essential for pollen tube pulsant elongation.
CaM plays a vital role in regulating pollen tube development and growth, and that CaM oscillation at the tip is required for the pulsant growth of the pollen tube.
CaM is involved in the control of pollen tube growth and the oscillation in the tip-to-base distribution pattern of CaM is necessary for the normal pulsatile growth of pollen tubes.

the function and distribution of CaM in the pollen tube and provides a useful tool for further research on the mechanism of Ca2+-calmodulin signal pathway in pollen tube development.

CaM is a vital factor to pollen tube growth, which is closely associated with the pulsant tip growth mode.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CaM was essential for pollen tube growth and CaM–GDP fusion protein was a useful tool to study CaM function in vivo.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the tip-to-base distribution of CaM in growing pollen tubes is a dynamic process, and the oscillations of tip-to-base distribution pattern of CaM are required for the normal growth of pollen tubes.
CaM is involved in pollen germination and tube growth and its oscillation in the pollen tube apex is essential for pollen tube growth.
